chunks: Had God pleased to take a son, He could have chosen whom He liked from among those He has created. Glory be to Him. He is God, the one, the omnipotent.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God taking a son?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for refuting the Christian doctrine of divine sonship and the concept of divine incarnation (Hulul), affirming that God’s essence is entirely distinct from His creation. The rhetorical structure highlights that any 'son' would be a created entity, thus subject to God's will, whereas God is Al-Qahhar (The Dominant) over all such creations. This reinforces the principle of Tawhid al-Dhat, emphasizing God's absolute uniqueness and transcendence.
